_note: Facets the gate does not hold a screen to, each with the reason why.
A waiver is fidelity DEBT, recorded where it can be counted — never a
quiet loosening of an assertion. Keys are a facet name ('callouts',
'rail', 'counter', 'fields', 'buttons', 'layout', 'appbar', 'title') or
'facet:needle' for one item — prefer per-item, so the rest of the facet
stays asserted.
Every entry below was written from a measured run against a clean
story-seeded stack, not guessed.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE J3 SCREENS WAVE (crest/j3-screens, Phase A):
* Root cause 1 — 'the reference's J3 rail does not exist' — is GONE for
the dashboard frames. The console now navigates by the reference's own
rails (Work status · Quality · Payments · Proof · Reports for
p2_11–p2_16; the five-entry setup rail for p1_* and p2_1–p2_7,
p2_17–p2_21), so every rail waiver on p2_11/p2_14/p2_15 is deleted
rather than re-argued. It survives only where a screen genuinely lives
in another door or another persona's console (p2_20 in the field door,
p2_21 in the custodian's).
* Root cause 2 — reference callout prose written over a fixture world —
is now recorded PER CALLOUT instead of per screen, so the callouts the
implementation does carry verbatim are asserted. What remains waived is
of two kinds, and the reason on each says which: prose that narrates
fixture data no deployment reproduces ('the 96 workers…', 'sitting
sent-back for 29 days', 'Ten held rows'), and one EXTRACTION artifact —
docs/journey-spec.json's callout text puts the bolded metric name after
the sentence it opens ('looks better if slow records are excluded…
Confirmed-paid percentage Guarded by …'), because
tools/journey-trace/extract-spec.py collects a node's own text before
its children's. No faithful screen can contain that word order; the fix
belongs in the extractor, and the waiver names it rather than hiding it.
Deleting a waiver is the unit of fidelity work. Nothing here loosens the
gate's rules — each entry is a named piece of unbuilt design, unwritten
copy, or a tool defect, and `make fidelity` counts them every run.

g1_3.buttons:Save and continue: MISSING ACTION named on the screen, not a copy difference: the reference's consent screen saves edited consent rules, and this deployment has nothing to save — the consent floor is enforced infrastructure read back, and scripts/templates are deployment configuration (#59), which the screen states on its face. The walk button says Continue because a 'Save' over nothing would fake a write, the exact class of dishonesty the G-1 wave refused (same rule g1_2 states verbatim for its own 'Save and continue').

g4_2.fields:Work email domain: MISSING CAPABILITY, named: the reference's review detail shows the work email domain with a uniqueness hint ('No other organisation uses this domain'), and no domain check exists in this deployment — the registration does not surface the work email and nothing verifies a domain against other organisations. The screen's 'What this does not prove' callout carries the reference's own caution about what the domain check would and would not establish; drawing the field without the check behind it would be inventing evidence on the screen that decides an admission.
g4_2.buttons:Approve the request: Unwritten copy, one word-form: the decision card is titled 'Approving the request' and its action reads 'Approve and publish' — the same single decision, labelled with its full consequence (approval publishes the organisation to the registry in the same transaction, under the decider's name). The reference's exact imperative 'Approve the request' appears nowhere in that word order; the control itself is real and asserted end to end through POST /v1/organisations/{id}/decision.

g2_1.callouts:This is the one answer that bra: Unwritten copy, one clause: the screen carries this callout's title and every sentence after the first, but opens 'The kind is the one answer that branches' where the reference opens 'This is the one answer that branches' — the implementation names the field because its callout sits in a sidecar away from the form, where the reference's deictic 'This' points at nothing. The rule the callout teaches is stated verbatim; the debt is the opening two words.

g2_4.callouts:Terms and projects are differen: Unwritten copy, measured the day #179 gave the gate a flow arrival: the implemented status screen (shared by g2_4 and g2_13) does not carry the reference's Done-stage callout distinguishing what your terms allow from what a project grants. A real copy gap on a real, reachable screen — the callout's body was already recorded below as an extractor artifact, but the title is missing because the callout itself is; closing this waiver means writing the callout, not touching the gate.
g2_4.callouts:Your terms say what you do. A p: EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, not a copy gap: extract-spec.py collects a node's own text before its children's, so the bolded emphasis words the reference sets inside this callout ('may' and 'will') comes out moved after the sentence it belongs in. No faithful screen can contain that word order; the fix is in the extractor (same defect the p2_14 waiver records), and this waiver names it rather than hiding it. Recorded now, while the screen itself sits quarantined behind #179, so the debt is already counted when the quarantine lifts.

A real copy gap on a real, reachable screen; closing it means writing the callout on the approved state, not touching the gate.
g2_13.callouts:You still cannot put your own n: The body of the missing 'One thing still not unlocked' callout above — one gap, two facet keys, both counted until the copy is written.
g2_13.buttons:Copy the key: MISSING CONTROL, not a copy difference: the reference's approved frame offers copying the organisation's key (its public identifier) and the implemented status screen has no such affordance. Named as an unbuilt control — it needs a decision about which key the screen surfaces (the org DID is on-screen; a key is not) before it can need a button.

w1_19.appbar: The spec's appbar reads 'CREST Console' because the reference sets this frame in a console mock; the worker door is the same shell honestly named for whoever holds it — 'CREST · Worker'. The product name differs by door, not by omission.
w1_19.callouts:They can already see your recor: Live-count prose, one word: the screen carries the callout's title and first sentence verbatim, then 'only about the N lines above' with the live disclosure list's real length — the reference's 'four' is its worked example, and the count Grace's record produces depends on how many credentials the walks have issued her. Asserting 'four' would assert the fixture, not the design.

w1_15.layout: The reference draws this consent moment as a phone frame; the worker door is deliberately a desktop console (appbar + sidebar at the gate's 1280px viewport) that keeps the phone experience under 720px. One decision surface serves w1_15+w1_19 — the two reference frames draw the same moment in two idioms — and the ledger records the console surface, so the phone-frame check is waived rather than the door redrawn.

w1_20.appbar: Same as w1_19: the reference mocks a console appbar; the worker door names itself 'CREST · Worker'.
w1_20.callouts:You can open this again any tim: Live-count prose: the screen carries the callout's title and first sentence verbatim, then the worker's real asked/agreed counts, and names the reference's twelve/nine on-screen as the worked example it is. Asserting those numbers would fake a history the record does not hold.

w1_7.layout: The reference's phone frame is served in the worker door's console idiom (appbar + sidebar at the gate's viewport, phone under 720px) — same waiver as w1_15, same reason.
w1_7.counter:Step 5 of 5: The reference places nomination as step 5 of the phone enrolment flow; the implementation is the worker's standing profile surface (#/profile/recovery), reachable any time — a stepper counter here would fake a flow position the screen does not have. The enrolment-time nomination the counter belongs to is real in the field door's confidence route (w1_4's 'Add a recovery contact now').

w4_1.layout: The reference draws the confirmer's request as an SMS on a phone; this deployment has no SMS channel (#150, Blueprint §16) and the same request is delivered in-app in the worker door's console idiom, with the channel gap stated on the screen itself.

w4_2.layout: Same as w4_1: the reference's phone/SMS frame, served in-app in the worker door's console idiom, the channel gap stated on-screen.

w4_3.layout: Same as w4_1: the reference's phone/SMS frame, served in-app in the worker door's console idiom.

w1_4.layout: The reference draws assisted enrolment on the agent's phone; the field door is a console shell (appbar + sidebar at the gate's viewport) that becomes the phone experience under 720px — the same cross-idiom placement p2_20's waivers record for this door.

w1_17.appbar: Same as w1_19: the reference mocks a console appbar; the worker door names itself 'CREST · Worker'.

p2_20.appbar: The reference frames evidence intake as a console screen for the Project Configurator; the implementation puts it in the FIELD door (docs/journey-traceability.md records the surface as field `#/roster`), whose appbar reads 'CREST · Field'. Cross-door placement is real fidelity debt — the row-by-row check itself is the part that is implemented.
p2_20.rail: The reference's five-entry J3 console rail now exists (p1_*/p2_* setup frames render it), but this screen is not in the console at all: the field door carries its own agent nav. Closing this waiver means building the configurator's own console-side intake-file frame, not renaming anything.
p2_20.callouts: Root cause 2 — the reference's callout names the fixture definition version ('WD-4471 v1.2') and its five specific checks as narration. The field screen states the rule in its own words ('The file is checked against the definition. A row that does not match becomes somebody named in the unclear queue — never a silent drop.'), which the forbidden-content rule for the sibling screen p2_21 holds to.
p2_20.buttons:Accept 306, hold 6: The label quotes the fixture's own counts. The implementation's action is 'Close the roster', which posts the real batch; the reference's per-file accept/hold verdict wording is unbuilt copy, not a missing capability.
p2_20.buttons:Reject the whole file: A whole-file rejection does not exist: the evidence service accepts a batch and holds the rows that fail. Named here as a MISSING ACTION rather than a copy difference — it needs an endpoint before it can need a button.

p2_21.rail: The custodian console's rail is the custodian's own five views (Find a worker · Duplicates · Unclear rows · Recoveries · Overdue reviews), not the reference's J3 rail — this screen is reached as the registry custodian, whose whole flow is a different journey. Cross-persona placement debt: closing it means the configurator's own console-side view of held rows, not a rail rename.
p2_21.callouts:The last one is the failure mod: Fixture narration ('the last one', 'Ten held rows') over a specific queue. The screen carries this callout's title and states the same gap in its own numbers-free words, because the count belongs to the reference's walkthrough, not to any deployment. The gap itself is real and unbuilt: nothing watches for a source that quietly went to zero.
p2_21.buttons:Open the first one: The unclear queue is a table where every row is openable and each carries its own 'Attribute' action; the reference's single 'open the first one' affordance is a walkthrough device, not a control the screen is missing.

p2_14.callouts:looks better if slow records ar: EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, not a copy gap: the spec's callout text carries the bolded metric name ('Confirmed-paid percentage') after the sentence it opens, because extract-spec.py collects a node's own text before its children's. The screen renders the reference's sentence in the reference's order, which cannot contain this word order. The fix is in the extractor.
p2_14.callouts:The row that crosses a boundary: The callout exists only to narrate one fixture row ('the 96 workers with no valid payment details'). The screen states the rule the callout is about — that a delay reason can belong to another team's list — through the owner named on every delay row instead.
p2_14.callouts:The 96 workers with no valid pa: Fixture narration: specific counts from the reference's walkthrough world. The cross-boundary fact it teaches is on the screen as the owning office on each reason, which is the part a deployment can be truthful about.
p2_14.buttons:Open the 17: The label quotes the fixture's own count of held instructions. The implementation lists every held instruction with its reason and owner in the table below the tiles, which is the substance the affordance existed for.

p2_15.callouts:You can see this without asking: The screen carries this callout and its title, with one word changed: 'she has worked on two' becomes 'she may have worked on two', because no deployment knows how many projects the worker in front of you has worked on. Asserting the reference's clause would be asserting the fixture. The consent posture itself — this project's own records need no consent, another project's needs a narrower disclosure — is stated verbatim.
p2_15.callouts:One row worth acting on: The callout narrates one fixture row ('sitting sent-back for 29 days'). The trail shows every hop's real state instead; a screen that invented a stale row to have something to point at would be worse than the missing callout.
p2_15.callouts:The last row has been sitting s: Fixture narration, same root as its title above.
p2_15.buttons:Export the bundle: There is no bundle export: no endpoint produces a portable proof bundle. A missing capability, named — not a copy difference.

n1.layout: The gate's desktop idiom requires an appbar AND a navigation rail. n1 is the door: nothing is scoped until somebody has signed in, so it deliberately renders the appbar alone — the design spec says so in as many words (docs/design/j3-connective-tissue/README.md: 'appbar only (no rail — nothing is scoped yet)'). The debt is in the gate's idiom vocabulary, which cannot express 'appbar only', not in the screen; a rail added here to pass this facet would be a rail over nothing.

g2_5.callouts:whether organisations register: EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, not a copy gap: extract-spec.py collects a node's own text before its children's, so this callout's bolded phrases ('which organisation', 'which country', and the emphasised subject of 'stood behind the work') come out moved after the sentences they belong in. No faithful screen can contain that word order; the screen carries the reference's real copy. Same extractor defect the g2_4 and p2_14 waivers record; recorded now, while the screen sits quarantined behind #179, so the debt is already counted when the quarantine lifts.
